text:
mira: Heads up — started seeing 502/503 from eu-west1 edge about 10m ago. Traffic to edge-api (svc=edge-api-prod) is being dropped intermittently.

mira: Errors look like backend connection reset, but only for requests coming through our ALB -> NLB path. Direct requests to nodeport are fine. :thinking:

sam: do we have recent deploys? any config changes on alb/nlb?

mira: no deploys in the last hour. Last infra change was a security group tweak yesterday to tighten source ports for the ALB healthchecks.

ryan: @mira can you paste the SG and NACL entries you're seeing? Also any ALB logs?

mira: ALB access log snippet:
```
2024-10-04T12:07:34Z alb-123 10.0.2.5:443 - - 502 - 0 0 - "GET /api/v1/ping" "curl/7.68" 123 0 0 - - -
```

mira: SG inbound rules (relevant):
```
Type: HTTPS  Protocol: TCP  Port: 443  Source: sg-alb
Type: Custom TCP Protocol: TCP  Port range: 1024-65535  Source: sg-alb
```

mira: NACL (subnet-edge) has ephemeral ports restricted:
```
Rule 100: ALLOW TCP 443 0.0.0.0/0
Rule 110: DENY TCP 1024-65535 0.0.0.0/0
```

alexa: aha — NACL denies high source ports for ephemeral responses. ALB/NLB healthchecks or backend connections might use high source ports when proxy protocol or port translation is in play.

sam: We recently enabled NLB in front of the ALB to preserve client IPs, and we also turned on proxy protocol on the NLB. That will change source-port behavior.

josh: If NLB/ALB stack rewrites source ports, the NACL DENY range would block return traffic. Should open ephemeral range or restrict rule to expected cidr rather than 0.0.0.0/0.

ryan: Quick mitigation: add allow rule for ephemeral ports for the ALB/NLB LB subnet (or sg-alb) then monitor.

mira: Trying a quick test — patching NACL to allow 1024-65535 from the ALB subnet (10.0.8.0/24) only. Rolling in 1m.

ops-bot: change-applied: Updated NACL subnet-edge rule 110 -> DENY removed, Rule 115 added ALLOW TCP 1024-65535 Source 10.0.8.0/24 by josh at 2024-10-04T12:20:10Z

mira: After the change, HTTP 200s are returning for the failing requests. Looks stable so far. :thumbsup:

sam: We should document this edge case — when layering ALB+NLB+proxy_protocol the source port can be ephemeral and NACLs that deny high source ranges will break traffic.

ryan: Agreed. Action items:
- Update infra runbook with ALB+NLB/ProxyProtocol NACL guidance
- Add test to e2e that exercises ALB->NLB path with proxy protocol
- Revisit NACL defaults to avoid 0.0.0.0/0 denies for ephemeral ranges

mira: I'll open a PR for the runbook and link the change here.

josh: Also adding a console alert when backend 5xx rate > 1% for more than 2 min for edge-api.

mira: PR: https://git.redwood.internal/r/redwood/infra/merge/42 — contains NACL note + recommended SG pattern.

alexa: Nice sleuthing team. Leaving notes in postmortem channel once PR merges. :eyes:
